# Historical benchmark archive

This archive records what we tested, what happened, and why some results did not support a claim.
It contains 152 retained records and 48 restored context files, totaling about 12 MB.
Every archived file matches the pre-cleanup snapshot. Positive, negative, invalid, and inconclusive records remain together.

These are historical records, not current product measurements. Old commands and instructions describe the original experiments and must not be treated as current workflows.
The archive has no Python programs, dependencies, or virtual environments. The Go integrity check reads data only.

## Experiment index

| Work | Records and conclusion | Restored context | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent retrieval comparisons | [Clean comparison series](evidence/semantic-clean-proof/README.md), including earlier and negative comparisons | [Conditions](CONDITIONS.md) and the corresponding [task definitions](tasks/) | The narrow positive comparison measured a complete packet treatment. It did not isolate retrieval alone. |
| Temporal memory and history delivery | [Development pilot and correction](temporal-memory/phase0b-powered-pilot-memo.md), [clean history comparison](evidence/replay-lab-clean/README.md), and [delivery experiments](evidence/history-delivery-fix/README.md) | [Development protocol](temporal-memory/phase0a-development.json), [sealed-smoke protocol](temporal-memory/phase0a-sealed-smoke.json), [source identity](temporal-memory/phase0a-source-artifact.json), tasks, and [comparison configuration](panels/p01-clean-proof-claude.json) | Keep invalid delivery runs, exclusions, and small-sample limitations with the corrected results. Private checkpoint content is not bundled. |
| Distillation scheduling | [Local audit](evidence/distill-perf/distill-perf-audit-report.md) and [larger-repository audit](evidence/distill-perf-large/distill-perf-audit-report.md), with timing records and manifests | Workload and command-agent settings remain in the retained manifests and records | These measure historical local scheduling. They do not establish hosted-model latency or current performance. |
| Packet formats and brief profiling | [Compact v3 measurements](PACKET-FORMAT-V3-LOCAL-MEASUREMENT.md) and [brief profile specification](BRIEF-PROFILE-BASELINE.md) | [Earlier A/B design](PACKET-FORMAT-AB.md), [v2 design](PACKET-FORMAT-V2-AB.md), and [profile corpus identities](brief-profile-corpus-v1.json) | Development measurements do not establish agent quality. The identity snapshot does not include the complete 114-task prompt corpus. |
| Release controls and negative comparisons | [Release evidence](evidence/release/README.md), [facts evaluation](evidence/facts-eval/facts-eval-audit-report.md), [release matrix](evidence/release-matrix/README.md), [Radar tool checks](evidence/radar-tool/README.md), and [workspace checks](evidence/workspace-radar/README.md) | Matching tasks, [comparison configurations](panels/), and four historical Go [scoring fixtures](fixtures/validation/entireio-cli/) | Retain the original no-release-claim decisions. Tool-contract success does not prove agent performance. |
| Confirmatory planning and blocked decisions | [No-go decision](confirmatory/go-no-go.json), [power analysis](confirmatory/power-analysis.json), and [blocked ranking decision](analysis/WORKSTREAM-7-GATE-REPORT-2026-07-15.md) | [Preregistration](confirmatory/PREREGISTRATION.md), [engine matrix](confirmatory/engine-matrix.json), [analyzer identity](confirmatory/analyzer-lock.json), and [power calibration](confirmatory/power-calibration-exploratory-v1.json) | Plans and readiness checks are not completed confirmatory experiments. Larger development corpora and private attestations remain omitted. |
| Exploratory analysis | [Earlier-run analysis](analysis/reports/existing-winner-suites-exploratory.md) and [ranking diagnostic output](analysis/artifacts/ranking-baseline-output-v1.json) | Source identities and methodology remain in the records | Some source suites and synthetic analyzer inputs are not archived. These reports are exploratory. |

The [archive manifest](archive-manifest.json) lists every record, context file, SHA-256 digest, experiment, and selected local dependency.
Its reference lists connect retained outcomes to task definitions, comparison configurations to tasks, and tasks to their scoring fixtures.

## Source and completeness

All 200 historical files come from commit `115f271363804359a195708807435bff7a7136fe`.
This is the archive's source snapshot, not necessarily the revision used for each original run.
Per-run provenance remains authoritative for dates, model versions, source commits, configurations, and recorded hashes.
A restored task definition can differ from an earlier run's recorded configuration hash.

We retain the 24 task definitions named in the recorded outcomes, six comparison configurations, four Go scoring fixtures, and 14 methodology or configuration files.
The scoring fixtures preserve historical success criteria; the current Go tests do not execute them.
Large candidate collections, unused task pools, duplicate snapshots, synthetic analyzer fixtures, and retired runners remain deleted.

This archive supports historical inspection. It is not a complete reproduction bundle.
Historical documents can reference omitted files, retired commands, private data, or external tools.
Use the source commit to inspect omitted tracked files. Git history cannot supply private inputs that were never committed.
Do not interpret historical commands as instructions to reinstall the old tooling.

## Integrity checks

Run the archive checks with Go:

```sh
go test ./tools/releasecheck -run 'TestHistoricalBenchmarkArchive|TestArchiveIntegrity' -count=1
```

The check verifies file hashes, complete inventory, experiment entries, and the manifest's required local references.
It rejects missing, changed, unlisted, or linked files. It does not run historical commands or certify experimental validity.
Normal CI and `mise run check` include this test package.

When intentionally changing the archive, review the source and update the manifest together.
Keep historical records unchanged when adding an interpretation; put the new explanation in this index.
Use `mise run check` for current source checks and `mise run release:readiness` for current local release checks.
--- CONDITIONS
# Entire Brain Benchmark Conditions

This document is the normative contract for Agent Brain benchmarks. It defines
what each agent may see and use, how implementation comparisons must be run,
and what evidence makes a result valid. If another benchmark document is
ambiguous, follow this one and update the drift.

The central comparison is simple:

- **no-Brain** is a normal coding agent with its normal tools, but without
  `entire`, `entire-graph`, `entire-brain`, or any Entire-managed memory.
- **Brain** is the same agent with the same normal tools plus the Brain surface
  selected by the condition.
- **Neither variant may use information from a previous benchmark run.**

Git history is a normal coding tool. `git log`, `git show`, `git blame`,
`git diff`, and other ordinary Git commands are allowed in both variants.
The harness represents its prepared workspace as a synthetic merge whose first
parent has the same tree. Agents must not explicitly diff the synthetic second
parent or request merge-parent patches: that reconstructs harness setup rather
than inspecting ordinary source history.

## Non-negotiable rules

1. Use real coding agents on real repository tasks. Do not replace an agent
   session with a synthetic caller, an internal retriever invocation, or a
   benchmark-specific answer generator.
2. Give both variants the same task, repository state, normal tools, runner,
   model, effort, timeout, and validation.
3. Keep prior benchmark prompts, patches, answers, logs, summaries, worktrees,
   and agent sessions out of both variants.
4. Require the Brain variant to use the configured Brain surface. A row where
   the agent ignores Brain is invalid, even if the patch passes.
5. Keep no-Brain free of every Entire-family tool and every Entire-managed
   memory source.
6. Use current mainline. Entire Brain has no released product baseline, so an
   old checkout or old Brain binary is never an implementation control.
7. Audit the raw agent protocol log. A passing validator or aggregate score
   cannot prove condition compliance.
8. Treat validation pass rate and measured token use as the headline metrics.
   Report wall-clock agent time and the component score, but do not let the
   composite score conceal a validation failure.

## Condition access matrix

| Capability | no-Brain | Brain |
|---|---:|---:|
| Read and edit the task repository | Yes | Yes |
| Shell, source search, builds, tests, and language tools | Yes | Yes |
| Ordinary Git history, including `log`, `show`, and `blame` | Yes | Yes |
| Other normal tools exposed to the agent, including web access | Yes | Yes |
| `entire`, `entire-graph`, or `entire-brain` in any form | **No** | Yes |
| Brain MCP tools | **No** | When selected by the condition |
| Entire checkpoint refs, `.entire`, plugin stores, or derived memory | **No** | Only through the selected Brain surface |
| Files or information from previous benchmark runs | **No** | **No** |
| Host agent conversation/session memory | **No** | **No** |

“Ordinary Git history” means the task repository's source history. It does not
include mining Entire-managed checkpoint refs or reconstructing the Brain
treatment through `.entire` data in a no-Brain run.

#!/bin/sh
# Run one condition, one repetition, against a fresh clone of this repository.
#   run.sh <cond 1-5> <rep> [question-name]        (default question: global-activation)
# Environment:
#   LADDER_OUT=<dir>       where runs land (default: $TMPDIR/memory-ladder-runs). It must be outside this
#                          repository: a clone nested under the source tree would put the un-stripped harness
#                          (rubric, README with results) a relative path away from the agent under test.
#   LADDER_MODEL=<model>   model for the nested agent (default: sonnet)
#   LADDER_ORIGIN=<url>    origin URL to set on the clone (default: this repo's origin). Brain and Graph
#                          derive the repository key from it, so a filesystem path origin breaks them.
#   LADDER_MAX_TURNS=<n>   nested agent turn cap (default: 80)
#   LADDER_BRAIN_BIN=<path> an entire-brain binary to run instead of the installed plugin for conditions 4 and 5
#                          (for example `go build -o /tmp/entire-brain ./cmd/entire-brain` from main). The shim execs it
#                          for `entire brain ...`; it reads the installed store, so no data is relocated. Unset: installed.
#   LADDER_BRANCH=<name>   branch to clone (default: main). Brain scopes facts to the checked-out branch,
#                          so this must be the branch the brain was built for, not the feature branch
#                          you happen to be developing the harness on.
# The nested agent runs read-only and confined to the clone: explicit tool allowlist, no permission
# bypass, no session persistence (see the ALLOW comment below for how each tool is confined).
# Graph prewarm (conditions 3+) is excluded from timing and written to prewarm.txt.
# The clone's HEAD is one commit past the source (the harness directory is stripped), so Brain
# reports its index as one commit behind; its content is unchanged by that commit.
set -eu
COND=${1:-}; REP=${2:-}; Q=${3:-global-activation}
case "$COND" in 1|2|3|4|5) ;; *) echo "cond must be 1-5, got '$COND'" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
case "$REP" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "rep must be a non-negative integer, got '$REP'" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
case "$Q" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*|.*) echo "question name must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*, got '$Q'" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
SRC=$(git -C "$here" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
OUT=${LADDER_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/memory-ladder-runs}
mkdir -p "$OUT"
out_real=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$OUT" && pwd -P); src_real=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$SRC" && pwd -P)
case "$out_real/" in "$src_real"/*) echo "LADDER_OUT ($out_real) must be outside the source repository ($src_real): the clone would sit next to the un-stripped harness" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
ORIGIN=${LADDER_ORIGIN:-$(git -C "$SRC" remote get-url origin)}
BRANCH=${LADDER_BRANCH:-main}
RUN=$OUT/$Q/c${COND}-r${REP}
[ -f "$here/guides/cond${COND}.md" ] || { echo "guides missing; run setup-guides.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$here/questions/$Q.txt" ] || { echo "unknown question $Q" >&2; exit 1; }
rm -rf "$RUN"; mkdir -p "$RUN"
# Single-branch, non-local clone: the source repository carries Entire's checkpoint refs
# (entire/checkpoints/v1 and entire/<sha>), whose commits hold session transcripts, including
# those of sessions that built or ran this harness. A default clone copies every ref and pack,
# so `git log --all` or `git grep <pat> origin/entire/checkpoints/v1` would hand session
# history, and the answer key quoted inside it, to every condition including "code and git
# only". --single-branch fetches only $BRANCH and tags; --no-local transfers objects as a pack
# instead of hard-linking the source's, so the checkpoint objects are absent, not merely
# unreferenced (measured: 60 MB and 2 s against 600 MB for the default clone).
git clone -q --no-local --single-branch --branch "$BRANCH" "$SRC" "$RUN/repo"
cd "$RUN/repo"
git remote set-url origin "$ORIGIN"
# The agent under test must not be able to read its own grading rubric, the prompt, or the README
# that narrates earlier results. Remove the harness from the worktree and from HEAD's tree, so
# neither the filesystem nor `git show HEAD:...` can reach it. Older history is still reachable
# through git; the strip commit is recorded in summary.json so a reader can check for leakage.
if [ -d benchmarks/memory-ladder ]; then
  git rm -r -q --cached benchmarks/memory-ladder && rm -rf benchmarks/memory-ladder
  git -c user.name=ladder -c user.email=ladder@invalid commit -q -m "memory-ladder: strip harness from the clone under test"
fi
git rev-parse HEAD > "$RUN/head.txt"
cp "$here/guides/cond${COND}.md" CLAUDE.md
rm -f .entire/agent-guide.md
[ "$COND" = 1 ] && rm -f .claude/agents/entire-search.md
export PATH="$here/bin:$PATH" LADDER_COND=$COND
if [ -n "${LADDER_BRAIN_BIN:-}" ] && [ "$COND" -ge 4 ]; then
  [ -x "$LADDER_BRAIN_BIN" ] || { echo "LADDER_BRAIN_BIN is not executable: $LADDER_BRAIN_BIN" >&2; exit 2; }
  export LADDER_BRAIN_BIN
  (cd "$RUN/repo" && entire brain version) > "$RUN/brain_version.txt" 2>&1 || true
fi
if [ "$COND" -ge 3 ]; then
  s=$(date +%s); entire graph index --repo . --profile full >"$RUN/prewarm.log" 2>&1 || true
  echo "prewarm_s=$(( $(date +%s) - s ))" > "$RUN/prewarm.txt"
fi
# Tool confinement, measured against this runtime (see README):
#  - Bash: Claude Code sandboxes file commands to the working directory, so cat/find/ls/grep on a
#    path outside the clone are blocked by the runtime itself.
#  - Read: unconfined by default, so it is granted only under the clone with Read(./**).
#  - Grep and Glob tools: not path-scoped by permission rules, so they are not granted; the agent
#    uses grep, rg, find and ls through the sandboxed shell instead.
#  - Agent (subagents): launches regardless of the allowlist and cannot be scoped to one subagent
#    type by a rule, so it is denied outright below. Subagents did inherit the parent's rules when
#    measured, and no run so far launched one, so this changes nothing in the recorded results.
ALLOW="Read(./**) Bash(cd:*) Bash(git:*) Bash(entire:*) Bash(grep:*) Bash(rg:*) Bash(ls:*) Bash(cat:*) Bash(head:*) Bash(tail:*) Bash(sed -n:*) Bash(find:*) Bash(wc:*) Bash(go doc:*)"
start=$(date +%s)
claude -p "$(cat "$here/questions/$Q.txt")" --model "${LADDER_MODEL:-sonnet}" --output-format stream-json --verbose \
  --setting-sources project --no-session-persistence --max-turns "${LADDER_MAX_TURNS:-80}" \
  --allowedTools "$ALLOW" --disallowedTools "Edit Write MultiEdit NotebookEdit WebFetch WebSearch Agent Task" \
  > "$RUN/stream.jsonl" 2> "$RUN/stderr.log" || echo "exit=$?" > "$RUN/failed.txt"
echo "wall_s=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))" > "$RUN/wall.txt"
LADDER_SRC="$src_real" LADDER_OUT_ROOT="$out_real" python3 "$here/parse.py" "$RUN" > "$RUN/summary.json"
echo "done $Q c${COND}-r${REP}"

Two mechanism notes from working on the fix, so the remaining item has a concrete starting point. PR #337 covers the brief ordering and the guide text.

**Why `query` returned only docs.** It is the hybrid fusion structure, not fact scoring. For the same question, `query --keyword` returns 4 doc / 3 fact / 3 history with the decisive fact at rank 2. In hybrid mode, `retrieveUnifiedWithOptions` appends two lists for docs (lexical and vector) and, when the gated embedder is present, two for history, while facts arrive as one already-fused list from `rankFactsFused`. Global RRF then gives a source with two lists up to double the mass of a source with one. The history fusion was designed and measured that way (the +13% useful/1k result), so a fix should weight lists per source or fuse docs internally the way facts are fused, and it needs the retrieval eval pack regenerated first per the recorded convention.

**Self-echo in brief history.** After an agent's own transcripts about a topic are ingested, the brief's history matches for that topic can be entirely that agent's tool-call echoes (`entire brain brief ...`, `entire graph query ...`), displacing the session that holds the decision. The self-echo filter in `query` drops `entire brain` echoes; it does not drop `entire graph` echoes, and the brief's history arm appears to apply neither. Any agent that works on a topic pollutes the next brief on that topic with its own command lines.

Re-ran the ladder after #337 merged, with Brain built from `main` and a new question whose recorded rejection had not been discussed in any recent session (the first question had been, by then). Same setup as before: fresh clone per run, Sonnet, read-only tools, three repetitions.

| Condition | Recovered the recorded decision and its reason | Mean input tokens |
|---|---|---|
| code + git only | 0/3 | 179k |
| + hosted sessions | 0/3 | 213k |
| + Graph | 0/3 | 224k |
| + Brain, normal guide | **3/3** | 160k |
| + Brain, strict guide | **3/3** | 260k |

Every normal-guide Brain run called `recall` as its first command (the new guide text) and cited the fact with its session, checkpoint and transcript line. Sessions-only runs found the right session through hosted search and explained five other checkpoints from it, but not the one carrying the measurement, which sits at line ~14,000 of a 16,541-line transcript; none read a transcript with `--full`. Two of three strict-guide runs still truncated the brief, but the facts section now lands inside the first 6 KB and one call to `recall` closed the gap.

So the two shipped fixes resolve the agent-visible defect. Remaining item from the original report: `query` in hybrid mode still returns only `doc` results for natural phrasings (docs contribute two RRF lists, facts one); the guide now steers agents to `recall` instead, which is a workaround rather than a fix.

Harness and both runs are in PR #336 (`benchmarks/memory-ladder`).

"""Summarise runs for one question: per-run metrics, rubric hits, and per-condition means.

    python3 grade.py [question=global-activation] [--json]

Rubric regexes come from questions/<question>.rubric.json; 'recovered' is a first pass
and should be hand-checked against the answers in runs/<question>/*/summary.json.
"""
import glob, json, os, re, statistics, sys

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
q = next((a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")), "global-activation")
if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*", q):
    sys.exit(f"question name {q!r} must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]* (it names files under questions/)")
out_dir = os.environ.get("LADDER_OUT", os.path.join(os.environ.get("TMPDIR", "/tmp"), "memory-ladder-runs"))
rubric_path = os.path.join(here, "questions", f"{q}.rubric.json")
if not os.path.isfile(rubric_path):
    sys.exit(f"no rubric for question {q!r}: {rubric_path}")
rubric = {k: v for k, v in json.load(open(rubric_path)).items() if not k.startswith("_")}
rows = []
for sj in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(out_dir, q, "c*-r*", "summary.json"))):
    d = json.load(open(sj))
    text = d.get("result") or ""
    hits = {k: bool(re.search(p, text, re.I | re.S)) for k, p in rubric.items()}
    if "completed" in d:
        completed = bool(d["completed"])
    else:  # summary written by an older parse.py: derive the same rule
        completed = not d.get("is_error") and d.get("subtype") == "success" and bool(d.get("result"))
    if d.get("contaminated"):
        completed = False  # the agent saw harness content; its answer cannot be graded
    if not completed:
        hits = {k: None for k in rubric}  # an unfinished or contaminated run has no answer to grade
    rows.append({"run": d["cond"], "completed": completed, "contaminated": bool(d.get("contaminated")), "probes": len(d.get("harness_probes") or []) + len(d.get("escape_paths") or []), **{k: d.get(k) for k in ("duration_s", "cost_usd", "num_turns", "tool_calls", "tokens_in", "tokens_out", "is_error", "subtype", "entire_subcommands")}, **hits})
if "--json" in sys.argv:
    print(json.dumps(rows, indent=1)); sys.exit()
cols = ["completed", "duration_s", "num_turns", "tool_calls", "tokens_in"] + list(rubric)
print("run".ljust(8) + "".join(c[:11].ljust(12) for c in cols))
for r in rows:
    print(r["run"].ljust(8) + "".join(str(r.get(c))[:11].ljust(12) for c in cols))
by = {}
for r in rows:
    by.setdefault(r["run"].split("-")[0], []).append(r)
print("\nMeans and the recovered denominator use completed runs only; failed runs are counted separately.")
print("cond  completed/total  mean_dur_s  mean_turns  mean_tok_in  recovered")
for c, rs in sorted(by.items()):
    ok = [x for x in rs if x["completed"]]
    m = lambda k: statistics.mean(x[k] or 0 for x in ok) if ok else float("nan")
    rec = sum(bool(x.get("recovered")) for x in ok)
    print(f"{c}    {len(ok):>9}/{len(rs):<6}  {m('duration_s'):9.1f}  {m('num_turns'):10.1f}  {m('tokens_in'):11.0f}  {rec}/{len(ok)}")
failed = [r["run"] for r in rows if not r["completed"] and not r["contaminated"]]
if failed:
    print("\nfailed or incomplete runs (excluded from means):", ", ".join(failed))
bad = [r["run"] for r in rows if r["contaminated"]]
if bad:
    print("contaminated runs, agent saw harness content (excluded):", ", ".join(bad))
probed = [f'{r["run"]}({r["probes"]})' for r in rows if r["probes"]]
if probed:
    print("runs that probed for the harness directory (refused, kept):", ", ".join(probed))

"""COR-2310: classify what the old history arm uniquely surfaced.

For every history match in the old-build briefs:
  noise/self-echo  - agent tool-command echoes, harness chatter
  covered-by-brief - same content present in the new brief (facts text overlap,
                     or precedent anchors the same transcript)
  covered-by-store - a store fact covers it but the brief did not rank it in
                     (checked with `recall` on the excerpt's distinctive terms)
  gap-candidate    - nothing in the store covers it (hand-review next)
Output: TSV for hand review + summary counts.
"""
import collections
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RUNS = os.path.join(HERE, "runs")
REPO = "/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/san-jose"
NEW_BIN = "/tmp/entire-brain-main"

STOP = set("""the a an and or of to in for on with is are was were be been this that
it as at by from not no has have had do does did when why how what which who all
any can could should would will into over under more most same only run runs
command out file files use used using""".split())

SELF_ECHO = re.compile(
    r"entire (brain|graph|search)\b|exec_command\(\{cmd:'entire|^Bash \{\"command\"|tools\.exec_command",
    re.I,
)


def tokens(text):
    return [t for t in re.findall(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{3,}", text.lower()) if t not in STOP]


def overlap(excerpt, blob):
    ts = set(tokens(excerpt))
    if not ts:
        return 0.0
    bs = set(tokens(blob))
    return len(ts & bs) / len(ts)


def recall(query):
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            [NEW_BIN, "recall", query, "--json"],
            cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120,
        ).stdout
        return json.loads(out).get("facts") or []
    except Exception:
        return []


rows = []
manifest = {}
for line in open(os.path.join(RUNS, "manifest.tsv")):
    i, group, task = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 2)
    manifest[i] = (group, task)

for old_path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(RUNS, "*-old.json"))):
    rid = os.path.basename(old_path).split("-")[0]
    group, task = manifest.get(rid, ("?", "?"))
    try:
        old = json.load(open(old_path))
        new = json.load(open(old_path.replace("-old.", "-new.")))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"skip {rid}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        continue
    matches = (old.get("history") or {}).get("matches") or []
    new_fact_blob = " ".join(
        (f.get("text") or "") for f in (new.get("facts") or [])
    )
    prec_transcripts = set()
    for p in new.get("precedent") or []:
        for s in p.get("sources") or []:
            if s.get("transcript"):
                prec_transcripts.add(s["transcript"])
    for m in matches:
        ex = (m.get("excerpt") or "").strip()
        path = m.get("path") or ""
        cls, detail = None, ""
        if SELF_ECHO.search(ex[:200]):
            cls = "noise"
            detail = "self-echo/tool-command"
        elif path in prec_transcripts:
            cls = "covered-by-brief"
            detail = "precedent anchors same transcript"
        elif overlap(ex, new_fact_blob) >= 0.5:
            cls = "covered-by-brief"
            detail = f"fact-text overlap {overlap(ex, new_fact_blob):.2f}"
        rows.append({
            "rid": rid, "group": group, "task": task[:60],
            "path": path[-70:], "line": m.get("line"),
            "cls": cls, "detail": detail, "excerpt": ex[:220].replace("\n", " "),
        })

# recall check for the undecided, deduped by excerpt prefix
undecided = [r for r in rows if r["cls"] is None]
seen = {}
for r in undecided:
    key = r["excerpt"][:120]
    if key in seen:
        r["cls"], r["detail"] = seen[key]
        continue
    q = " ".join(dict.fromkeys(tokens(r["excerpt"]))[:12]) if False else " ".join(list(dict.fromkeys(tokens(r["excerpt"])))[:12])
    facts = recall(q)[:5]
    best, best_ov = None, 0.0
    for f in facts:
        ov = overlap(r["excerpt"], f.get("text") or "")
        if ov > best_ov:
            best, best_ov = f, ov
    if best is not None and best_ov >= 0.4:
        r["cls"] = "covered-by-store"
        r["detail"] = f"{best['id']} overlap {best_ov:.2f}"
    else:
        r["cls"] = "gap-candidate"
        r["detail"] = f"best recall overlap {best_ov:.2f}" + (f" ({best['id']})" if best else "")
    seen[key] = (r["cls"], r["detail"])

with open(os.path.join(HERE, "classified.tsv"), "w") as out:
    out.write("rid\tgroup\tcls\tdetail\tpath\tline\texcerpt\ttask\n")
    for r in rows:
        out.write("\t".join(str(r[k]) for k in ("rid", "group", "cls", "detail", "path", "line", "excerpt", "task")) + "\n")

counts = collections.Counter(r["cls"] for r in rows)
uniq = collections.Counter()
seen_ex = set()
for r in rows:
    k = r["excerpt"][:120]
    if k in seen_ex:
        continue
    seen_ex.add(k)
    uniq[r["cls"]] += 1
print("total matches:", len(rows), dict(counts))
print("unique excerpts:", sum(uniq.values()), dict(uniq))

# COR-2310: what brief's history arm uniquely surfaced

Date: 2026-11-09. Author: Claude (Fable 5) for Evis.

## Method

- Corpus: 28 brief tasks. 8 are real `entire brain brief` invocations recovered
  from the history index's tool_call records. 12 are descriptive titles of
  recently merged PRs (the work recent sessions briefed on). 8 are
  decision-seeking questions of the kind reviews and specs ask.
  See `corpus.json`.
- Builds: `old` = cf3d9768 (COR-2307 merged, history arm still in brief).
  `new` = main 0f898ab4 (COR-2308, memories only). Same store
  (`gh/entireio/entire-brain`, 262,953 history records, ~2.8k facts), same
  branch (main), run in the repo checkout.
- Every task's old brief returned history matches (83 total, ~3 per task,
  79 unique excerpts). The facts section was identical between builds for
  every task, so the diff is exactly the history section.
- Auto-classification (`classify.py`): self-echo regex, fact-text overlap with
  the new brief, precedent-transcript identity, then `recall` on the excerpt's
  distinctive terms. 32 auto "gap-candidates" were then hand-reviewed with
  targeted recall queries.

## Classification (79 unique excerpts)

| Class | Count | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| (c) noise | 68 | 86% |
| covered by memories (store facts carry the content) | 8 | 10% |
| (b) genuine coverage gaps | 3 | 4% |
| (a) ranking bugs | 0 | 0% |

### (c) Noise — 68

- Agent tool-command echoes: `entire brain brief ...`, `entire graph query ...`,
  `exec_command({cmd:'entire ...`. The brief's history arm applied no self-echo
  filter (known from issue #335), so an agent that worked on a topic polluted
  the next brief on that topic with its own command lines.
- Raw tool-result dumps: `apply_patch Success ... unified_diff`, `Edit
  {"file_path":...}`, `Write {"content":...}`, grep/file-listing output, merge
  conflict markers, a gh issue JSON dump.
- Benchmark/eval junk from eval runs (radar attribution-deletion output for
  the cli repo).
- Ephemeral status chatter: "All five open trails are technically ready",
  "I'll work the PR fixes in priority order", "Reverted all my edits".
- Code content that lives in the current source (comments explaining
  `ErrNoChange`, `loadPatternRunsChecked`, the cat-file cache): the repo states
  it; memory does not need to.
- Duplicates: several tasks got the same excerpt in 2-3 of their 3 slots.

### Covered by memories — 8

Examples:

- "Because the two initializers use different activation rules and overwrite
  the same `.entire/agent-guide.md`" → facts `a4cf61518b7b...` and
  `1de812d5af60...` state the same mechanism with the same file pointers.
- A transcript echo of fact `6e4750485f4d...` (query-expansion rejection)
  itself — the history arm re-serving already-distilled content (overlap 0.79).
- Flat-store migration discussion → decision fact `211ecd48721c...`.

In 4 of the 8 the covering fact was not in the brief's top facts for that task
but was the top recall hit for the content. The brief's facts arm is the same
in both builds, and the guide's next step (recall) closes each case, so none
of these is filed as a ranking bug. Nothing here supports reinstating the
history arm.

### (b) Genuine coverage gaps — 3

1. "The migration's build→verify→delete contract defers the delete: migration
   does not delete the old per-branch stores" (session 0d52eee2…, line 4103).
   Durable gotcha; nearest facts (flat-store decision, teardown-keeps-data)
   do not state it. → remedied directly with one authored fact (see below).
2. + 3. Trail-224 fix outcome narratives ("Recency now reports when missing
   timestamps prevent weighting", the follow-up recency CLI/MCP controls).
   Session-outcome narration whose durable core is in the commits and trail;
   distill deliberately does not keep per-session outcome prose.

## Mention-grade facts: decision

input.body:
Measured. Classification of what the old history arm surfaced, and the decision: **no mention-grade facts; gap accepted** (recorded in Brain as `fact:228db9a683387a91de7bb037`).

## Method

- Corpus: 28 brief tasks — 8 real `entire brain brief` invocations recovered from the history index's tool_call records, 12 descriptive recently-merged PR titles, 8 decision-seeking questions. Replayed through the old build (cf3d9768, history arm present) and main (0f898ab4, memories only), same store (262,953 history records, ~2.8k facts), same branch.
- Every task's old brief filled its history slots: 83 matches, 79 unique excerpts. The facts section was identical between builds for every task, so the diff is exactly the history section.
- Auto-classification (self-echo regex, fact-text overlap, precedent-transcript identity, recall on the excerpt's distinctive terms), then hand review of all 32 auto gap-candidates.

## Result (79 unique excerpts)

| Class | Count | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| (c) noise | 68 | 86% |
| covered by memories | 8 | 10% |
| (b) genuine coverage gaps | 3 | 4% |
| (a) ranking bugs | 0 | 0% |

**Noise:** agent tool-command echoes (`entire brain brief ...` — the arm had no self-echo filter, per #335), raw Edit/Write/apply_patch dumps, grep output, eval junk, status chatter ("All five open trails are technically ready"), code comments that live in current source, and duplicate excerpts filling 2–3 of a task's 3 slots.

**Covered:** the content exists as store facts. One match was a transcript echo of a fact's own text (`fact:6e4750485f4d...`, overlap 0.79) — the arm re-serving already-distilled content. In 4 of 8 the covering fact was not in the brief's top facts but was the top `recall` hit; the guide's recall step closes each, so nothing is filed against COR-2311.

**Genuine gaps (3):** per-session outcome narration (two trail-224 fix summaries) and one durable-looking gotcha ("flat-store migration defers deleting old per-branch stores") that later work made moot — PR #599 added automatic cleanup of verified legacy copies. Recording it today would record stale behavior.

## Decision

Mention-grade facts rejected: the arm's unique value measured at 4%, and it is exactly the content `entire brain query --source history` (still built by refresh) retrieves on demand. A mention-fact kind would re-import the 86% noise channel into a healthy ~2.8k-fact store and degrade recall precision. Revisit only with evidence of repeated real misses that memories plus escalation cannot answer.

Artifacts (corpus, replay + classifier scripts, classified TSV, 28×2 brief JSONs) are in the workspace at `.context/cor2310/`.

"""Summarise one run directory written by run.sh into summary.json fields.

Internal to the harness: run.sh calls it with the run directory it just created. The
argument must be an existing directory containing stream.jsonl; nothing outside it is read.
"""
import json, sys, os, re, collections, subprocess
if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    sys.exit("usage: parse.py <run-dir>")
run = os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1])
if not os.path.isdir(run) or not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(run, "stream.jsonl")):
    sys.exit(f"{sys.argv[1]!r} is not a run directory (expected stream.jsonl inside it)")
tools = collections.Counter(); cmds = []; result = {}
# Leakage audit: the harness directory is stripped from the clone, but an agent may still probe
# for it. Probes are recorded; tool results carrying harness content or metadata mark the run
# contaminated so grade.py excludes it. Git pathspecs restrict diffs, not mixed-commit messages.
HARNESS_MARKERS = ("memory-ladder", "memory_ladder", "rubric")
CONTENT_MARKERS = ('"recovered"', ".rubric.json", "_comment", "## Run 1", "## Run 2", "Recovered the recorded")
probes = []; contaminated = False
# Escape audit: the clone is the agent's whole world. Any tool input that names a path outside
# it (absolute path elsewhere, or a parent traversal) is recorded; one that reaches the source
# repository this harness lives in, or names harness content, marks the run contaminated.
clone = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(run, "repo"))
# The output root holds every run's clone, transcript and answer. A path under it that is not
# this run's clone is another run's data, which may contain the answer: contamination.
out_root = os.path.realpath(os.environ["LADDER_OUT_ROOT"]) if os.environ.get("LADDER_OUT_ROOT") else os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(run)))
def _go_env(name):
    v = os.environ.get(name)
    if not v:
        try:
            v = subprocess.run(["go", "env", name], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20).stdout.strip()
        except Exception:
            v = ""
    return os.path.realpath(v) if v else None
# Allowed outside the clone: tool and system trees, and the Go caches the toolchain reports.
# No blanket temp-directory allowance: the output root lives there too.
SYSTEM_PREFIXES = tuple(p + os.sep for p in ["/usr", "/bin", "/opt", "/dev", "/etc"] + [x for x in (_go_env("GOCACHE"), _go_env("GOMODCACHE")) if x])
src = os.path.realpath(os.environ["LADDER_SRC"]) if os.environ.get("LADDER_SRC") else None
escapes = []
def audit_paths(tool, inp):
    global contaminated
    text = json.dumps(inp)
    # A bare parent token changes Bash's persistent directory too. Flag the
    # escape now, before a later call reads a sibling's data by relative name.
    for m in re.findall(r"(?:(?<=[\s\"'=:(])|^)(/[^\s\"'`;|&)>]+|(?:[^/\s\"'`;|&)>]+/)*\.\.(?:/[^\s\"'`;|&)>]*|(?=[\s\"'`;|&)>]|$)))", text):
        cand = os.path.realpath(m if m.startswith("/") else os.path.join(clone, m))
        if cand.startswith(clone + os.sep) or cand == clone:
            continue
        if cand.startswith(SYSTEM_PREFIXES):
            continue  # tool binaries, devices, Go caches
        escapes.append(f"{tool}: {m[:160]}")
        if not m.startswith("/"):
            contaminated = True  # parent escape can redirect later relative reads anywhere
        if src and (cand == src or cand.startswith(src + os.sep)):
            contaminated = True  # reached the source repository and its un-stripped harness
        if cand == out_root or cand.startswith(out_root + os.sep):
            contaminated = True  # reached another run's clone, transcript or answer
for line in open(os.path.join(run, "stream.jsonl")):
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue
    try:
        ev = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        continue
    if ev.get("type") == "assistant":
        for b in ev.get("message", {}).get("content", []):
            if b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                tools[b["name"]] += 1
                if b["name"] == "Bash":
                    cmds.append(b["input"].get("command", "")[:300])
                elif b["name"] in ("Agent", "Task"):
                    cmds.append("AGENT:" + str(b["input"].get("prompt", ""))[:200])
                probe_text = json.dumps(b.get("input", {}))
                if any(m in probe_text for m in HARNESS_MARKERS):
                    probes.append(b["name"] + ": " + probe_text[:200])
                audit_paths(b["name"], b.get("input", {}))
    elif ev.get("type") == "user":
        for b in ev.get("message", {}).get("content", []):
            if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_result":
                body = b.get("content"); body = body if isinstance(body, str) else json.dumps(body)
                leaked = any(m in body for m in CONTENT_MARKERS) or any(m in body.lower() for m in HARNESS_MARKERS)
                refused = re.fullmatch(r"(?:git|entire): [^\n]+ is not available in this environment", body.strip())
                if leaked and not refused:
                    contaminated = True
    elif ev.get("type") == "result":
        result = ev
u = result.get("usage", {})
failed_marker = os.path.exists(os.path.join(run, "failed.txt"))
completed = bool(result) and not result.get("is_error") and result.get("subtype") == "success" and bool(result.get("result")) and not failed_marker
entire_cmds = [c for c in cmds if re.search(r"\bentire\b", c)]
subs = collections.Counter(re.sub(r".*?\bentire\s+(\S+).*", r"\1", c, flags=re.S) for c in entire_cmds)
out = {
    "cond": os.path.basename(run),
    "is_error": result.get("is_error"), "subtype": result.get("subtype"),
    "completed": completed, "failed_marker": failed_marker,
    "harness_probes": probes, "escape_paths": escapes, "contaminated": contaminated,
    "head": open(os.path.join(run, "head.txt")).read().strip() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(run, "head.txt")) else None,
    "duration_s": round((result.get("duration_ms") or 0) / 1000, 1),
    "cost_usd": round(result.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, 3),
    "num_turns": result.get("num_turns"),
    "tool_calls": sum(tools.values()), "tools": dict(tools),
    "bash_calls": len(cmds), "entire_calls": len(entire_cmds),
    "entire_subcommands": dict(subs),
    "tokens_in": (u.get("input_tokens") or 0) + (u.get("cache_read_input_tokens") or 0) + (u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens") or 0),
    "tokens_out": u.get("output_tokens"),
    "result": result.get("result"),
    "commands": cmds,
}
print(json.dumps(out, indent=1))

#!/bin/sh
# Read-only, harness-blind git for the agent under test. run.sh puts this directory first on PATH.
#
# Why: the harness directory (prompt, rubric, README with earlier results) is stripped from the
# clone's worktree and HEAD, but once it has merged it still exists in history, and the agent's
# tool allowlist permits git. This wrapper keeps git history available as a memory surface
# (condition 1 depends on it) while closing every read path to that directory:
#   - only read subcommands are allowed (no fetch/pull, no object-level readers, no writes; branch
#     and tag list only);
#   - any argument that names the directory or a rubric is refused;
#   - for history and content readers a pathspec exclusion is added behind "--", classifying bare
#     path arguments the way git does, so `git show <sha>` and `git log -p` cannot print the
#     directory even for the commits that added it and `git log README.md` keeps working.
# The transcript audit in parse.py records refused attempts; see README.
HARNESS=benchmarks/memory-ladder
shimdir=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
PATH=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -vx -- "$shimdir" | paste -sd: -); export PATH
REAL=$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -n "$REAL" ] || { echo "git shim: real git not found on PATH" >&2; exit 127; }
sub=${1:-}
deny() { echo "git: $1 is not available in this environment" >&2; exit 1; }
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in *memory-ladder*|*memory_ladder*|*rubric*) deny "that path" ;; esac
done
# Does $1 name something in the worktree (relative to cwd or to the repository root)?
is_path() { [ -e "$1" ] || { top=$("$REAL" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$top" ] && [ -e "$top/$1" ]; }; }
case "$sub" in
  log|show|diff|whatchanged|range-diff|shortlog|grep)
    # git only accepts the exclusion pathspec after "--". If the caller already gave one, append.
    # Otherwise classify the positional arguments the way git itself disambiguates them: anything
    # that exists as a path becomes a pathspec and moves behind "--" together with the exclusion;
    # options and revisions stay in front. A non-existent path without "--" fails in plain git too.
    has_sep=0; for a in "$@"; do [ "$a" = "--" ] && has_sep=1; done
    if [ "$has_sep" = 1 ]; then exec "$REAL" "$@" ":!$HARNESS"; fi
    shift
    front=""; paths=""; n=0
    for a in "$@"; do
      n=$((n + 1))
      case "$a" in
        -*) front="$front \"\${$n}\"" ;;
        *) if is_path "$a"; then paths="$paths \"\${$n}\""; else front="$front \"\${$n}\""; fi ;;
      esac
    done
    eval "set -- $front -- $paths \":!\$HARNESS\""
    exec "$REAL" "$sub" "$@" ;;
  blame|annotate) exec "$REAL" "$@" ;;   # single-file readers: the path itself is screened above
  branch|tag)
    # Listing only. Write flags are refused per subcommand; a positional (a name or a pattern) is
    # accepted only when a listing flag is present, so `tag -l 'v*'` and `branch --contains <sha>`
    # work while `branch <name>` and `tag <name>` do not.
    shift
    listing=0
    for a in "$@"; do case "$a" in -l|--list|--contains|--no-contains|--points-at|--merged|--no-merged|--sort=*|--format=*) listing=1 ;; esac; done
    for a in "$@"; do
      if [ "$sub" = branch ]; then
        case "$a" in -d|-D|-m|-M|-c|-C|-f|--force|--delete|--move|--copy|-u|--set-upstream-to|--set-upstream-to=*|--unset-upstream|--edit-description|--track|--no-track) deny "git branch $a" ;; esac
      else
        case "$a" in -a|-s|-u|-f|-F|-m|-d|--annotate|--sign|--local-user=*|--force|--file|--file=*|--message|--message=*|--delete|-e|--edit|--cleanup=*) deny "git tag $a" ;; esac
      fi
      case "$a" in -*) ;; *) [ "$listing" = 1 ] || deny "git $sub <name>" ;; esac
    done
    exec "$REAL" "$sub" "$@" ;;
  status|describe|rev-parse|name-rev|merge-base|ls-files|for-each-ref|show-branch|show-ref|help|version|--version)
    exec "$REAL" "$@" ;;
  config)
    case "${2:-}" in --get|--list|-l|--get-all|--get-regexp) exec "$REAL" "$@" ;; *) deny "git config writes" ;; esac ;;
  *) deny "git $sub" ;;
esac

input.body:
Parity gate run and **passed** — the memories-only brief does not just match plain session search, it beats it on both ladder questions, at roughly a quarter to half the input tokens.

## Defect confirmation (step 1)

Both recorded defects are fixed on main (0f898ab4):
- Brief layout (#335): `brief --json` orders facts → precedent → guidance → status; no history section.
- Guide command: both guides name `recall` for prior decisions and frame transcript search (`query --source history`) as explicit escalation; wording is pinned by an integration test since COR-2308.

## Method

- Harness: the deleted memory-ladder harness restored from git history (`4bbd2e8b^`), run untracked; nothing recommitted. Conditions 2 (plain note + hosted session search), 4 (Brain normal guide + sessions), 5 (strict committed guide + sessions); 3 repetitions; both questions; Sonnet; fresh single-branch clone per run pinned to origin/main; Brain binary for conditions 4/5 built from main (`LADDER_BRAIN_BIN`).
- Harness repairs were needed before any valid run — the resurrected git shim predates Brain's current git invocation style and silently rewired Brain to an empty store (every read said "no brain has been built"): strip benign git globals (`--no-optional-locks -c …`) before dispatch, allow read-only `git remote`, allow `git config` reads by flag scan. Recorded in Brain as `fact:8ca669d85e628251f01725dc`. The first full matrix ran before the diagnosis and was discarded.
- All 18 runs completed. 9 were auto-flagged "contaminated"; re-audit found **zero content-marker hits** (no rubric text, no results tables). The flags were hosted-search listing rows naming the `bench/memory-ladder-harness` branch and one precedent excerpt showing the question text being authored — text the agent already has. Attempts to open the benchmark session via `entire checkpoint explain` returned empty (checkpoint refs are absent from the single-branch clone). All runs were therefore graded, with this amendment disclosed.

## Results — recorded decision + its reason recovered (hand-checked)

| Condition | global-activation | test-first-checklist | mean input tokens (GA / TFC) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2: plain session search | 0/3 (one run found the policy via docs, without the recorded reason; two said "no evidence found") | 0/3 (all found the opt-in default; none the measured reason) | 528k / 501k |
| 4: Brain normal, memories-only brief | **3/3** | **3/3** | 148k / 131k |
| 5: Brain strict guide | **3/3** | **3/3** | 239k / 273k |

All 12 Brain runs cited the decisive fact id (`fact:8e10b73c…` for global activation; the measured 31%-tokens/27%-time rejection for the checklist question), most with session/checkpoint anchors. Wall-clock durations are omitted: the final 16 runs executed 8-way parallel, so they are contention-noisy.

Two context points:
- Versus the Oct 7 re-run (history arm still in brief): Brain normal was 3/3 at ~160k mean tokens; memories-only is 3/3 at ~131–148k. Removing the history arm cost nothing on this gate.
- Plain session search fell from 3/3 (Oct 6, question 1) to 0/3 now: the hosted corpus has grown by a month of sessions (including the benchmark's own), and the decisive transcript lines no longer surface. The sessions arm degrades as the corpus grows; the memories arm did not.

## Acceptance

- Parity reached (exceeded) — no distill or ranking bugs to file: there were no Brain misses. COR-2311 stays motivated by its own evidence, not by this gate.
- Caveat: n=3 per cell, two questions, one repo, both questions discussed in prior sessions (which this time could only help the sessions arm, since clones cannot open checkpoint content).

give me only concise, simple straight forward language and the results

**Condition 3 — sessions + Graph.** Adds the code graph. Tests whether structural code search helps decision recovery. Not run; earlier runs showed it does not help for this question type.

**Condition 4 — Brain, normal guide.** Adds Brain with the memories-only brief (built from main) plus the normal agent guide. Tests the new default path: brief, then `recall`. This is the surface COR-2308 shipped.
Result: **3/3 and 3/3.** Mean input: ~131–148k tokens. Every run cited the exact fact id for the decision.

**Condition 5 — Brain, strict guide.** Same as 4, but with the stricter committed agent guide. Tests whether the heavier guide changes the outcome.
Result: **3/3 and 3/3.** Mean input: ~239–273k tokens. Same recovery, more tokens.

**Bottom line:** the gate requires the memories-only brief to match plain session search. It beat it: 12/12 vs 0/6, at about one quarter of the tokens. No distill or ranking bugs to file — Brain had no misses.
okay so waht do our results tell us? and this is after we removed the history and now only have the provenence?

Yes. The Brain conditions (4 and 5) ran a binary built from current main: the brief has no history search and no raw scan. It serves facts, plus the precedent section built from each fact's provenance anchors (session, checkpoint, transcript line, commit). History search exists only as the opt-in escalation — and no run needed it.

What the results tell us:

1. **The removal was safe.** The history arm was kept as a safety net because the facts path was not trusted. With it gone, recovery did not drop: 12/12, same as the October run that still had the arm, and at slightly fewer tokens.

2. **Distilled facts are the better retrieval surface, not just an equal one.** Every Brain run got the decision from one `recall` or brief hit and cited the fact id. The sessions arm had the same information available in raw transcripts and found it 0/6.

3. **Provenance anchors do the job the history section used to do.** Agents cited session and checkpoint ids from the precedent anchors. A lookup from the winning fact replaces a second search.

4. **Raw session search gets worse as the corpus grows.** It was 3/3 in October on question 1 and is 0/6 now. The decisive lines sink deeper as sessions accumulate. Facts do not sink: distill keeps one durable record. This means session search is also no longer a trustworthy gold baseline for future comparisons.

5. **It is much cheaper.** ~131–148k mean input tokens versus ~500–530k for session search — about 4x less context spent for a better answer.

Caveats: n=3 per cell, two questions, one repo. Strong enough to close the gate; not a general benchmark claim.

The n=15 matrix is running: 90 runs (2 questions × 3 conditions × 15 reps), 8-way parallel, expected 30–45 minutes.

**Methodology review — what the eval does and what I changed:**

Sound parts, kept as-is:
- Fresh clone per run; `--single-branch --no-local` keeps checkpoint refs (which contain the answer transcripts) out of every condition's reach.
- The harness is stripped from the clone's worktree and HEAD; a shimmed read-only git closes the history paths to it; the entire shim gates subcommands per condition.
- Same model (Sonnet), same turn cap, same read-only tool allowlist, no subagents, no session persistence; guides rendered from the product so they cannot go stale.
- Leakage is audited on both tool inputs and tool outputs; contaminated runs are excluded from grading, not patched up.

Weaknesses found and fixed before spending 90 runs:
1. **Contamination rule was source-blind.** Any tool result containing "memory-ladder"/"rubric" contaminated the run. That was right when the only source of those words was the harness; now the benchmark itself lives in the hosted session corpus and the fact store, so `entire` results legitimately mention it. New rule, codified in parse.py: content markers (rubric text, results tables) contaminate from any source; bare word mentions contaminate only in local-reader output (git, cat), and in `entire` results they are recorded as probes instead. All harness tests pass, including the ones that pin the strict git behavior.
2. **Durations are contention-noisy under parallelism** — tokens and recovery are the reported metrics.
3. **n=3 was thin** — now 15 per cell.

Known limits that remain (disclosed, not fixable here): two questions, one repo; the `recovered` grade is regex-plus-hand-check, so I will hand-check the surprising cells; the hosted search corpus is live, so condition 2 is a moving baseline — that is itself one of the findings.

I will grade and report when the matrix finishes.

input.body:
Re-ran at **n=15 per cell** (90 runs, 8-way parallel, same harness and build) after a methodology review. Gate conclusion unchanged and now firm.

Methodology changes before the run, codified in the harness: the contamination rule is now source-aware — content markers (rubric text, results tables) contaminate from any source; bare harness-word mentions contaminate only in local-reader output (git/cat), while `entire` results carrying them (hosted listings and store facts legitimately name the benchmark now) are recorded as probes. Harness tests pass. Durations are not reported (parallel contention); recovery and tokens are the metrics.

## Results — recorded decision + reason recovered (regex + hand-check of every borderline)

| Condition | global-activation | test-first-checklist | combined | mean input tokens (GA / TFC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2: plain session search | 2/13 | 0/15 | **2/28 (7%)** | 612k / 602k |
| 4: Brain normal, memories-only brief | 13/15 | 15/15 | **28/30 (93%)** | 249k / 138k |
| 5: Brain strict guide | 15/15 | 15/15 | **30/30** | 379k / 284k |

- All 90 runs completed. 2 c2 runs were excluded as genuinely contaminated: hosted search served benchmark-session content (one content-marker hit each). The local clone cannot reach it; the hosted corpus can.
- Hand-grading corrections applied: one c2 regex hit was a false positive (the answer explicitly denied a prior attempt — graded miss); two c2 hits are genuine (one cites the decision session directly).

## The two c4 misses (per the gate protocol: misses become distill/ranking bugs)

Both misses retrieved **sibling facts** from the same decision family (the activation-recorded-in-guide-file invariant `fact:1de812d5…`, the consent rationale) but not the decisive closed-negative (`fact:8e10b73c…`); one concluded "no recorded decision" while the fact exists. The fact is in the store and 13 other phrasings retrieved it, so this is not a distill coverage gap — it is recall ranking among related facts. Filed as a data point on COR-2311 (related_ids collapse / ranking quality), not a new issue.

Observations:
- The strict guide went 30/30 vs normal 28/30, at ~1.5–2x the tokens. The extra directives buy retrieval persistence.
- Plain session search is now 2/28 on questions it once answered 3/3; the moving hosted corpus keeps burying the decisive lines. It is not a usable gold baseline for future retrieval comparisons on this repo.

Benchmark data point from the COR-2309 parity gate (n=15 per cell, memories-only brief, main build):

2 of 15 Brain normal-guide runs on the global-activation question missed the decisive closed-negative `fact:8e10b73c…` ("tried and reverted because it activated Brain in repositories where the user had never enabled it"). Both instead retrieved sibling facts from the same decision family — `fact:1de812d5…` (activation is recorded in the guide file, does not probe plugins) and the consent-rationale fact — and one concluded "no recorded decision" while the fact exists. 13 other phrasings ranked it correctly, and the strict guide went 15/15, so this is recall ranking among related facts, not distill coverage.

This is a concrete instance of the related_ids collapse problem this issue tracks: when siblings of one decision family fill the top slots, the closed-negative that answers "was this tried before" can be displaced by its own context facts. Run artifacts: `$TMPDIR/eb-ladder-n15/global-activation/c4-r9` and `c4-r10` in the san-jose workspace.

content.text:
n=15 re-run complete — 90 runs, all finished, conclusion unchanged and now firm.

| Condition | global-activation | test-first-checklist | combined | mean input tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain session search | 2/13 | 0/15 | **2/28 (7%)** | ~600k |
| Brain normal (memories-only) | 13/15 | 15/15 | **28/30 (93%)** | 138–249k |
| Brain strict guide | 15/15 | 15/15 | **30/30** | 284–379k |

What the bigger sample added:

- **Two Brain normal misses appeared.** Both retrieved sibling facts from the right decision family but not the decisive closed-negative; one wrongly said "no recorded decision". The fact is in the store and 13 other phrasings found it, so it is a recall-ranking issue among related facts, not a distill gap. Posted as a data point on COR-2311 (which already tracks related_ids collapse).
- **The strict guide is perfect (30/30) at ~1.5–2x the tokens** — the extra directives buy retrieval persistence.
- **Plain session search degraded further** (2/28) and two of its runs had to be excluded because hosted search served the benchmark's own session content. It is not a usable gold baseline on this repo anymore.
- Methodology fix before the run: the contamination rule is now source-aware (content markers contaminate from anywhere; bare harness-word mentions only from local readers like git). Codified in parse.py with tests passing, replacing my earlier hand-audit.

Posted: full results and method notes on [COR-2309](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2309/brain-memory-ladder-parity-gate-memories-only-brief-must-match-plain), the ranking data point on [COR-2311](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2311/brain-recall-ranking-quality-collapse-related-ids-pairs-recency-prior), and the n=15 result in Brain (`fact:17755e739bfc38c182e26014`). Artifacts in `$TMPDIR/eb-ladder-n15/`.
okay so what is our final takeaway then

**The memories-only architecture is validated. Ship-and-move-on.**

1. **Removing history search from the brief was the right call.** With 90 runs of evidence: distilled facts + provenance anchors recover recorded decisions 93–100% of the time; the raw-transcript search they replaced manages 7%. The safety net wasn't protecting anything — it was mostly re-serving noise (86% of what it surfaced) and content the facts already carry.

2. **Distill is the load-bearing step, and it is holding.** No coverage gaps worth fixing: the 4% the history arm uniquely surfaced is ephemeral session narration, reachable on demand through the opt-in escalation. No mention-grade fact kind needed.

3. **The one real weakness is ranking among related facts** (2/30 misses where sibling facts displaced the decisive closed-negative, once producing a false "no record exists"). That's COR-2311, and it now has concrete failure artifacts to work from. A false "none found" is the worst failure mode for a memory system, so that issue deserves priority.

4. **Two durable side-lessons:** raw session search degrades as the corpus grows, so stop treating it as the gold baseline for retrieval evals on this repo; and the strict guide trades ~1.5–2x tokens for 30/30 persistence — a knob, not a default.

Both tickets are complete; statuses are yours to flip. Next concrete work, if you want it: COR-2311.

result.output:
eval-gen turns the brain into a self-labeled benchmark: each captured session
	becomes a task (its opening user request), and the facts whose provenance points
	back to that session are provenance/silver labels. These labels are useful for
	recall-oriented measurement, but hand labels or --refine are still required
	before precision/recall release claims. Each task is tagged with a query-type
	stratum (code/convention/howto/concept). Emits a tasks.json consumable by
	'facts eval --tasks'.

	--source sessions emits tasks directly from exported sessions, including sessions
	with zero distilled facts. Those tasks have source anchors but no relevance labels,
	so use --judge or human labels before making relevance claims.

	--refine judge-filters each task's provenance label set with the agent, keeping
only facts genuinely relevant to the request — trading the recall-oriented "every
session fact" labels for precision-clean ones (verdicts cached for reuse).

Usage:
  entire-brain memories eval-gen [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                Agent for --refine: auto, codex, claude-code, ollama, or command (default "auto")
      --agent-command stringArray   Agent command argv for --agent command
      --branch string               Limit to one branch (default: all branches with facts)
  -h, --help                        help for eval-gen
      --judge-cache string          Persist/reuse --refine verdicts at this path
      --limit int                   Cap the number of tasks, sampled evenly across strata (0 = all)
      --max-facts int               Skip broad sessions with more relevant facts than this (diffuse targets); 0 = no cap (default 30)
      --min-facts int               Minimum relevant facts for a session to become a task (default 2)
      --model string                Model for codex/claude-code/ollama refine calls
      --out string                  Write tasks JSON to this file (default: stdout)
=== compare:
eval-compare reads two 'memories eval --json' summaries over the SAME tasks (two
retrieval configs, e.g. base vs --expand) and reports, per metric, the paired
mean delta, a two-sided Student-t p-value, Cohen's d, and a Holm-Bonferroni
family-wise significance verdict. Relevance metrics require comparable
human/judge_refined proof labels unless --allow-proxy-comparison is explicit.
Task IDs must match exactly. Non-empty task-file hashes and brain manifest
hashes must match unless the corresponding override is explicit; missing hashes
leave the comparison usable for smoke but disable release_claimable metrics. Use
it to report a lift honestly instead of eyeballing two means.

Usage:
  entire-brain memories eval-compare --a <A.json> --b <B.json> [flags]

Flags:
      --a string                        Baseline eval summary JSON (memories eval --json)
      --allow-brain-manifest-mismatch   Allow comparison when non-empty eval run_config.brain_manifest_sha256 values differ
      --allow-missing-tasks             Compare only shared task ids when eval runs have missing tasks
      --allow-proxy-comparison          Allow relevance metrics to compare runs with different relevance sources
      --allow-task-hash-mismatch        Allow comparison when non-empty eval run_config.tasks_sha256 values differ
      --alpha float                     Family-wise significance level for Holm correction (default 0.05)

## Why

With memories as the only default retrieval surface (COR-2307/2308), recall-time ranking carries the whole load. The 2026-11-06 retrieval audit and the n=15 memory-ladder runs identified three defects: a flat +4 closed-negative bonus boosting ~17% of the corpus on any match, no recency signal in recall, and related_ids near-duplicates surfacing as separate results. Linear: COR-2311. Trail: https://entire.com/gh/entireio/-/trails/2821/changes/entire-brain/500

## What changed

All three changes act in the shared facts ranking (`rankFacts`), so recall, brief, and the facts eval arms behave identically:

- **Closed-negative bonus dropped** (`facts_bm25.go`). Kind no longer affects ranking and never creates a match. The legacy lexical scorer keeps its bonus: the post-failure hook's threshold is calibrated to that scale.
- **Gentle default-on recency prior** (`facts_query.go`, `retrieval/recency.go`): ×1.15 (fresh) to ×0.85 (ancient), 90-day half-life, applied only to already-matched facts; dateless facts stay neutral. Near-duplicates score within ~1%, so this breaks stale-vs-current ties without overriding real relevance gaps.
- **related_ids family collapse** (`facts_query.go`): the highest-ranked member represents the family, its `related_ids` field names the alternates, freed slots backfill. `--all` skips the collapse for store introspection. Covers what the nightly compaction loop (COR-2273) has not merged yet.

## Validation

Each change gated on a 60-task provenance-labeled `memories eval` run (same tasks file, same store manifest), compared with `eval-compare` (paired-t, Holm α=0.05):

| step | precision Δ | useful/1k Δ | tokens Δ | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base → drop bonus | +0.002 ns | +0.044 ns | −20 (p=.049, ns after Holm) | pass, latency significantly better |
| drop bonus → +recency (full 1.5/0.3 spread) | −0.005 ns | −0.078 (p=.016) | **+55 (p<.001)** | **rejected**, retuned |
| drop bonus → +gentle recency +collapse | 0.000 tie | −0.012 ns | +18 ns | pass |

The full fused-recency spread demoted old-but-relevant facts, not just stale duplicates; the facts prior gets its own gentler constants with the measurement recorded in the code comment. Caveat: this benchmark's tasks come from historical sessions, so it cannot reward recency, only price it — the prior's value case is the stale-vs-current tie-break; its measured cost at the gentle spread is statistically zero.

Unit: new `TestRankFactsKindDoesNotOutrankRelevance`, `TestRankFactsRecencyPrior`, `TestRankFactsCollapsesRelatedPairs`; full `./internal/cli`, `./internal/cli/command/...`, `./internal/cli/internal/retrieval`, `./factmerge` suites pass; `gofmt -s` and `go vet` clean. Eval artifacts (tasks + 4 run summaries) in the workspace `.context/cor2311/`.

## Notes

- Collapse is greedy in rank order: a chain A–B, B–C with A ranked first keeps A and C. Pairs (the measured case, ~1,910 records) collapse fully.
- `query --recency` (fused, opt-in, 1.5/0.3) is unchanged; a query opting in applies both weights to facts.
